Key observations from test image:
- Tomato leaf with yellowing/orange-brown necrosis at the tip/edge
- Dark black-brown necrotic lesion at the leaf margin
- Mottled/uneven green coloration on the rest of the leaf
- Small scattered dark spots on the green portions
- Leaf appears somewhat distorted

Top candidates: Late_Blight, Leaf_Mold, Early_Blight, Bacterial_Spot. Let me view references.

Analysis complete. Now let me compare findings:

**Test image features:**
- Dark brown-black necrotic lesion at the leaf tip/margin (~1/4 of leaf)
- Yellow-orange transition zone adjacent to the necrosis
- Rest of leaf is green with slight mottling
- Irregular, spreading lesion pattern from the margin

**Reference comparison:**
- **Late_Blight**: Dark brown-black lesions spreading from margins with yellow border — closely matches (especially bottom-right reference image)
- **Early_Blight**: Shows concentric ring "target" spots with yellow halos — rings not visible in test
- **Bacterial_Spot**: Many small discrete spots throughout leaf — doesn't match single large lesion
- **Target_Spot**: Very tiny scattered dots — doesn't match
- **Septoria_Leaf_Spot**: Small circular spots with light centers — doesn't match
- **Leaf_Mold**: Pale whitish-yellow patches — doesn't match dark necrosis

The test image shows a large irregular dark brown-black lesion spreading from the leaf margin with a yellow-orange transition zone — hallmark pattern of Late Blight.

This spreading, irregular marginal necrosis pattern is characteristic of Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans), matching the reference images which show similar dark brown-black lesions expanding from leaf margins. Early Blight was ruled out due to absence of concentric ring (target) patterns; other candidates don't match the single large marginal lesion morphology."}
